cards.name: Lot printed value 1
cards.flag: weak: printed value is swamped by Hype (Hype is 64% of all points)

ambiguities: Which lot does a second bidder get if the first bidder takes one: the other (assumed, stated in rules).
Round with zero Paddle-passers and an empty deck+discard: assumed no draw and no error (never reached in practice).
Does 'nobody draws' apply to the income step of all passers or only when short: assumed all passers (happened in 13.30% of 6p all-strategic games).
Reshuffle timing: assumed the discard is shuffled only when a player must draw from an empty deck (mid-draw, so some passers may draw before and some after).
Tiebreak 'bid value in hand' ties after cards-in-hand tie: shared win (assumed).
Hype tie for top category: all tied categories crash (as written); this happens in a visible share of games and is very swingy.
Bots treat hand sizes as public; Paddle vs Bid cards are indistinguishable face down, which does not matter in simulation.

problems.problem: Skill barely shows when several players play well: decisions do not separate good from random play at a mixed table.
problems.evidence: 3 strategic + 3 random (6p): strategic 17.8% vs random 15.5% per seat (5p: 20.3 vs 19.5). A lone strategic bot among randoms wins 28.6% (6p) / 36.6% (5p), a gap of 17.5 points, below the 20-point target. Best simple exploit found: pass 5 rounds then bid high, 26% at 6p vs random, but banking en masse loses (3 bankers: 4-8% each).
problems.fix: Give players information or leverage to act on (public hand sizes already exist; add a visible count of Paddles passed, or a second bid card choice), and make the bubble target readable earlier. Re-test E4 (bid 1-12) which lifted the lone-strategic share to 33% at 6p.

problems.problem: Hype swamps printed lot values: lot value is a minor part of the score.
problems.evidence: Hype is 55% (5p) / 64% (6p) of all points after the crash; printed values are ~40%. Lot value 1 has the weakest link to winning (corr 0.13 vs 0.27 for value 3). E1 (lots +2) lowers Hype share to 46-53% but raises unsold lots with strong bots (9.9 per game) and forced passes (34%).
problems.fix: Raise printed lot values moderately (e.g. 2-5, not +2 across the board) together with income 2, or accept Hype-driven scoring and say so in the pitch. Retest as a pair.

problems.problem: Tied bids and empty hands leave many lots unsold; some rounds are dead.
problems.evidence: Unsold lots per game: 5.2 (5p mixed), 4.6 (6p mixed), 7.8 (6p all-strategic) of 28; 15.6 bids per game are cancelled by ties (6p mixed). In the narrated game rounds 11 and 13 had zero bids and two lots worth up to 4 were wasted. Forced-pass (empty hand) rate is 23% of player-rounds; mean hand is 1.6 cards.
problems.fix: Income 2 per pass (E2): unsold 7.8 -> 6.4 and forced passes 22% -> 13% in the all-strategic table, last-round winner flips 29% -> 19%. Also consider unsold lots carrying to the next round.

problems.problem: Last round decides a lot: the final burn decides which category crashes and flips the winner.
problems.evidence: The leader before round 14 loses in 26% (5p) / 31% (6p) of games; the crash category changes in round 14 in 40% / 49% of games. Kingmaking is possible (a player out of contention can burn into a category), but this sim did not model deliberate kingmaking bots.
problems.fix: Hide nothing new: keep the swing but reduce it with income 2 (E2 flips 19%) or hand 5 (E5 flips 11% at 6p all-strategic, but runaway late 0.65).

problems.problem: Ties in the final score are fairly common.
problems.evidence: Shared/tied top score in 3.4% (5p mixed) to 4.3% (all-greedy 5p) of games, resolved by leftover cards.
problems.fix: Acceptable; tiebreaker is clear. E2 cuts ties to 0.2-1.2%.

problems.problem: Estimated length is at the low edge of the target.
problems.evidence: Estimated 16.3 min (14 rounds, my timing model: 25 s bid, 15 s reveal, 4 s per burned card, 6 s per lot, +3 min setup/scoring) vs 20 min target. With the designer's 70 s per round it would be 19.3 min. Real timing is untested.
problems.fix: Time with humans; if short, nothing to change.
